title: Money sent home
hook: Migrants send home more than all foreign aid and investment combined.
notes: World Bank Migration and Development Brief 40 (2024): ≈ USD 656 billion to low- and middle-income countries in 2023, larger than FDI and official aid combined (excl. China). Shares of GDP ≈ 2023, rounded. Flows drawn are major corridors, schematic.

scenes.title: A quiet giant
scenes.text: In 2023, migrants sent about 656 billion dollars to families in low- and middle-income countries. That is more than foreign direct investment and development aid combined.

scenes.title: The biggest receivers
scenes.text: India received about 120 billion dollars, more than any country in history. Mexico followed with about 66 billion, then China, the Philippines and Pakistan.

scenes.title: Where it matters most
scenes.text: In Tajikistan, money sent home is close to half of the whole economy, mostly from workers in Russia. In Nepal, Honduras and Lebanon, it is about a quarter.
